sections.title: False Prophets Denounced
observations: In this section, God addresses the false prophets of Israel who were misleading the people with their deceptive messages. They claimed to speak for God, yet their prophecies were not rooted in truth. This highlights the importance of discernment in spiritual leadership and the need for true prophetic voices that align with God's Word.

The imagery of a wall being built without proper foundation symbolizes the fragility of the false teachings. Just as a wall cannot stand without a solid base, so too can false prophecies not withstand the test of God's judgment.

sections.title: Judgment on the False Prophets
observations: God declares that He will bring judgment upon these false prophets. This serves as a warning that those who lead others astray will face severe consequences. It emphasizes God's commitment to truth and justice, ensuring that His people are not led into error.
The metaphor of the 'wind' signifies the emptiness of their prophecies. Just as wind cannot provide substance or security, so too do false prophecies lack the power to save or protect.

sections.title: The Role of Women in Prophecy
observations: This section introduces the concept of women who prophesy falsely, often referred to as 'diviners.' It raises important questions about the role of women in spiritual leadership and the dangers of manipulation and deceit in prophetic ministry.

The mention of 'bands of handkerchiefs' and 'veils' indicates the use of physical objects in their practices, which can be seen as a form of superstition rather than genuine faith. This serves as a reminder to evaluate the means through which we seek God's guidance.

importantVerses.commentary: They have misled my people, saying, 'Peace,' when there is no peace. This verse underscores the danger of false assurances and the responsibility of leaders to speak truthfully about God's judgment.

Because with lies you have made the heart of the righteous sad, whom I have not made sad. This highlights the emotional and spiritual damage caused by false prophets, emphasizing the need for truth to bring healing.

questions: What criteria should we use to discern true prophets from false ones?
How can we ensure that our spiritual leaders are grounded in the truth of Scripture?
What implications does this chapter have for the role of women in ministry today?
